title: Listing a garment for sale
description: What the server returns when the app asks for help selling a garment on Depop. Two calls: describe (photographs in, a draft listing's facts out) and prices (search phrases in, comparable listings and retail prices out). Both are proposals the app shows for the person to check and edit; nothing here decides a price — the arithmetic that turns comparables into an asking price and a net payout lives in the domain core, in Dart, where it is tested. Golden fixtures in contracts/examples/listing/ are parsed on both sides.

money.description: An amount in the currency's major unit (25.0 is twenty-five dollars). Only US dollars are carried: a seller in the US is priced against US listings, and a price in another currency is excluded rather than converted, because a comparable built on an invented exchange rate looks like evidence and is not.

searchQueries.description: What to search for. Written by the describe call from the photographs and editable by the person before prices are looked up, so a wrong guess about the brand is a typo to fix rather than a wasted search.

listingFacts.description: A draft of what a buyer needs to know, read from the photographs. Every optional property follows the scan contract's rule: absent means the photographs did not show it, never a guess presented as a reading.

title.description: Brand, item and the words a buyer searches for, most important first: 'Nike vintage crewneck sweatshirt grey'. Becomes the first line of the description.

brand.description: Read from a logo or a brand label. Wrapped with a confidence because a brand guessed from a swoosh-shaped print and one read off the neck label are different claims to put in front of a buyer.

material.description: As a composition label states it ('80% cotton, 20% polyester'). Absent unless a label was photographed: a fabric guessed from a photograph is not something to sell a garment on.

sizeOnTag.description: The size printed on the size label, exactly as printed ('M', 'W32 L30', 'UK 10'). Absent unless a size label was photographed.

styleWords.description: Search words a buyer would use: cut, era, style, print. No brand (it has its own field) and no filler ('nice', 'cool').

era.description: Only when the photographs show it (a dated label, an unmistakable cut): '90s', 'Y2K'. Absent otherwise.

visibleFlaws.description: What a buyer would complain about, said plainly: 'small mark on the left cuff'. Empty when none is visible, which is not a promise that none exists.

comparable.description: A listing on Depop for the same or a similar item. Every one came back from a web search made for this request, and its price was found in the text of that page — a comparable the server cannot point to is dropped, not shown.

sold.description: True when the page says the item has sold, false when it is still for sale. Absent when the page does not say. A sold price is what somebody paid; an asking price is what somebody hopes for, and the core weighs them differently.

condition.description: The condition as that listing states it, verbatim. Absent when it does not say.

match.description: 'same' when it is the same product (same brand and model), 'similar' when it is the same kind of thing from a comparable brand. Anything less alike is not returned at all.

why.description: One line on why it counts: 'Same Nike Club crewneck, also grey'.

retailReference.description: What the same or a similar item costs new, from a retailer or the brand's own shop. Never from a resale site.

excludedCounts.description: What the search found and the server would not show, by reason. Shown to the person so an empty list reads as 'nothing usable' rather than 'nothing looked'.

status.description: 'ok' — searched. 'notConfigured' — this server has no search key; the app falls back to links and prices typed in. 'quotaExceeded' — the search service's free allowance is used up for now. 'unavailable' — the search service failed or timed out. Every status but 'ok' comes with empty lists, and none of them is an HTTP error: a listing can still be written without a price search.

searchedAt.description: When the search ran, so a price checked three weeks ago says so. Present when status is 'ok'.

describeContext.description: Sent with the photographs as the multipart form field 'context' (a JSON string), when the garment is already in the wardrobe. What the app already knows outranks a fresh reading: a brand the person typed is not second-guessed from a photograph.

notes.description: Anything the person typed about it ('bought in 2019, worn twice').
